Subsectorspharma distribution pbm
TickersCVS WBA MRK LLY NVO
Geographynational
CoverageCPI item index for prescription drugs — the transaction price pharmacies RECEIVE from patients and insurers (including Medicare), priced from a ~4,700-outlet national sample.
If it movedThe price pharmacies receive. Falling drug CPI against rising hospital and physician CPI says the deflation is drug-specific - generic entry and channel, not health-care disinflation.
Statsobservations: 115 mo in our pull · latest: 550.590 (2026-07); -0.77% m/m, -3.06% y/y · units: index
GapsManufacturer REBATES paid after the transaction are excluded, so the fall overstates the change in NET prices. Published unadjusted — BLS serves identical values for the CUSR and CUUR ids, so there is no seasonally-adjusted variant despite the id existing. Generic substitution is captured by design, so much of a decline is patent cliffs, not policy.
Relevancehigh — the only monthly read on drug price direction; the pack charted hospital and physician prices rising while this line was missing entirely
Our seriescpi_prescription_drugs
NotesFRED does NOT carry this (verified 2026-08-17: series lookup returns HTTP 400 'does not exist' for CUSR0000SEMF01/CUUR0000SEMF01, and a 135-hit full-text search for 'prescription drugs' returns no CPI-family series). Hence dashboard/collectors/bls_series.py. v1 API tier is 25 requests/day — all bls series go out in ONE batched POST.

Hospital Provider Cost Report (HCRIS) ↗CMShospitals facilitiesIn dashboardannuala fiscal year is completfreehigh
PublisherCMS · Federal gov
Cadenceannual · lag a fiscal year is complete ~10-22 months after it ends (5-month filing deadline + CMS processing); CMS republishes the archives quarterly
Accesszip_scrape · zip
CMS HCRIS HOSP10FY<year>.zip archives (downloads.cms.gov/files/hcris), parsed by bond_credit/hcris.py into a per-hospital table (bond_credit/data/exports/hcris_hospital_year.csv); this repo reads that export
Subsectorshospitals facilities
TickersHCA THC UHS CYH
CoverageEvery Medicare-certified hospital (~5,800/yr; ~4,300-4,500 general acute-care after exclusions). Worksheet G-3 margins (operating margin, KH-style definition), S-3 Part I inpatient days by payer (payer mix = share of inpatient DAYS, not revenue), S-2 name/address.
If it movedIf the census median moves with Kaufman Hall's sample median (same direction, a stable gap), the monthly KH read can be trusted for the sector; if they diverge, KH's Strata sample is drifting from the population and its monthly prints should be discounted. A rising share of hospitals losing money in the census is the broad-distress signal no sample or bond panel can give. Medicare's share of inpatient days rising means more volume at payment rates below cost (MedPAC's Medicare margin is ~-12% to -13%).
GapsAnnual and lagged; staggered fiscal years (labelled by FY end year; the December year-end cohort is the calendar-year match); as-filed figures; most line-24 'other (specify)' revenue has generic labels and cannot be classified operating vs non-operating (5-6% of operating revenue, shown on the page); no Medicare margin yet.
Relevancehigh — benchmarks the KH sample vs the full universe; adds payer mix
Our serieshcris_op_margin_median
NotesBoard #629 phase 1 shipped 2026-10-20: census panel under the Kaufman Hall charts (dashboard/hcris_panel.py, collector dashboard/collectors/hcris_census.py). Medicare margin NOT built (needs worksheet D/E cost apportionment). Phase 2 = EMMA.

CoveragePer-NDC average price retail pharmacies actually PAY to acquire a drug, from a monthly survey of ~2,000+ pharmacies. The highest-frequency free drug-price series that exists anywhere.
If it movedWhat pharmacies PAY. Accelerating generic acquisition deflation temporarily EXPANDS pharmacy margin because reimbursement lags on the way down - and squeezes it when acquisition costs inflate on shortages.
Statsrows: 968,002 in the 2026 dataset alone · units: usd_per_unit
GapsRETAIL pharmacy acquisition cost — specialty and limited-distribution products are thin or absent (measured 2026-08-17: IMBRUVICA returns 0 rows, as do the generic/biosimilar molecule names APIXABAN, SEMAGLUTIDE, USTEKINUMAB, EMPAGLIFLOZIN and ETANERCEPT, while SITAGLIPTIN — a small-molecule generic — returns 56). So it reads the small-molecule generic-entry story well and the biologic story badly. Acquisition cost, not the retail or net price, and Medicaid-survey-based rather than all-payer. Naming is two-sided: brands appear under the brand name, generics under the molecule, and neither list alone is complete.
Relevancehigh — `classification_for_rate_setting` (G/B) plus the paired generic price make the generic-entry mechanism behind the 2026 CPI collapse directly measurable, 8 months timelier than anything else in the pack
NotesScoped and PRICED 2026-08-17, deliberately not built. The v1 cut: ~50 curated molecules (the IRA-negotiated 10, the GLP-1s, the largest recent patent cliffs), one server-side `starts with` query each, emitting a weekly median NADAC per molecule plus a brand-vs-generic spread. Measured, not estimated: 15 molecules took 39.5s (2.64s each) -> ~2min for 50 per run; 3,165 rows for 15 -> ~10.5k rows per run; the per-year dataset already holds all 32 weekly snapshots of 2026, so unlike the CMS quarterly file there is NO accrete-or-lose deadline. Corrects an earlier note in this file that priced this as a 1M-row NDC-crosswalk problem: server-side filtering means the full 968k-row file is never touched. Real cost is ~2h of collector (the shape is identical to cms_drug_spending) plus ~1-2h of one-time curation to verify both the brand and generic spelling of each molecule returns rows — and that list needs a match-report guard like `negotiated_match_report`, because a spelling that drifts silently drops a molecule from the median.

NotesREJECTED on effort, not on value. Revisit only if a free aggregation appears, or if the new CMS schema enforced from April 2026 makes the files genuinely uniform. TRIGGER CHECKED 2026-08-27 -- STILL REJECTED, and now on a better ground than effort. (1) Free aggregation: NO. Serif Health, Payerset, Turquoise and PayerPrice all gate bulk data behind paid tiers; PayerPrice's free items are lookups and an explorer, not a downloadable national aggregation. DoltHub hosts a transparency-in-coverage repo but not a maintained national hospital MRF corpus. (2) Uniform schema: NOT DEMONSTRATED. The spec did tighten -- CMS finalised new/removed MRF data elements and a strengthened attestation (45 CFR 180.50(a)(3)(iii)) in the CY2026 OPPS/ASC final rule, effective 2026-01-01 with enforcement from 2026-04-01. But a uniform SPEC is not uniform FILES, and no post-enforcement compliance measurement has been published. Careful with the number that circulates here: the widely-quoted "21.1% fully compliant" is PatientRights- Advocate NOVEMBER 2024 and says nothing about the 2026 schema. CMS is now auditing for accuracy, completeness and formatting rather than mere existence, which is itself evidence CMS does not yet treat the files as uniform. (3) NEW, and the reason to stop revisiting on the schema question: AHA's 2026-06-05 fact sheet notes the MRFs carry rates "without the algorithms and rules that health plans apply to those rates to generate the actual payment amount". So even a perfectly uniform file yields a negotiated rate, not a realised price. That is a STRUCTURAL limit, not an effort one, and it does not resolve with better schemas. AHA also notes the annual requirement churn itself impedes use -- and the CY2026 revision is the fourth, with CY2027 already in cycle. REVISIT CONDITION, REWRITTEN TO BE CHECKABLE (the old one was unfalsifiable prose and sat unwatched for four months after its own date passed): re-open ONLY on a named, dated event -- (a) a free bulk national MRF corpus with a maintained schema, or (b) a published post-2026-04 compliance study showing >80% conformance to the CMS template, or (c) CMS itself publishing a consolidated MRF dataset. Absent one of those, do not re-evaluate before 2027-04-01.
Inventoried2026-08-27

PublisherU.S. BLS · Federal gov

BLS public API v1 (POST, keyless); NOT on FRED
Subsectorspharma distribution pbm
TickersCVS WBA MRK LLY NVO
Geographynational
CoverageCPI item index for prescription drugs — the transaction price pharmacies RECEIVE from patients and insurers (including Medicare), priced from a ~4,700-outlet national sample.
If it movedThe price pharmacies receive. Falling drug CPI against rising hospital and physician CPI says the deflation is drug-specific - generic entry and channel, not health-care disinflation.
Statsobservations: 115 mo in our pull · latest: 550.590 (2026-07); -0.77% m/m, -3.06% y/y · units: index
GapsManufacturer REBATES paid after the transaction are excluded, so the fall overstates the change in NET prices. Published unadjusted — BLS serves identical values for the CUSR and CUUR ids, so there is no seasonally-adjusted variant despite the id existing. Generic substitution is captured by design, so much of a decline is patent cliffs, not policy.
Relevancehigh — the only monthly read on drug price direction; the pack charted hospital and physician prices rising while this line was missing entirely
Our seriescpi_prescription_drugs
NotesFRED does NOT carry this (verified 2026-08-17: series lookup returns HTTP 400 'does not exist' for CUSR0000SEMF01/CUUR0000SEMF01, and a 135-hit full-text search for 'prescription drugs' returns no CPI-family series). Hence dashboard/collectors/bls_series.py. v1 API tier is 25 requests/day — all bls series go out in ONE batched POST.

Hospital Provider Cost Report (HCRIS) ↗In dashboardfreeeffort: moderate
PublisherCMS · Federal gov

Accesszip_scrape · zip

Subsectorshospitals facilities
TickersHCA THC UHS CYH
CoverageEvery Medicare-certified hospital (~5,800/yr; ~4,300-4,500 general acute-care after exclusions). Worksheet G-3 margins (operating margin, KH-style definition), S-3 Part I inpatient days by payer (payer mix = share of inpatient DAYS, not revenue), S-2 name/address.
If it movedIf the census median moves with Kaufman Hall's sample median (same direction, a stable gap), the monthly KH read can be trusted for the sector; if they diverge, KH's Strata sample is drifting from the population and its monthly prints should be discounted. A rising share of hospitals losing money in the census is the broad-distress signal no sample or bond panel can give. Medicare's share of inpatient days rising means more volume at payment rates below cost (MedPAC's Medicare margin is ~-12% to -13%).
GapsAnnual and lagged; staggered fiscal years (labelled by FY end year; the December year-end cohort is the calendar-year match); as-filed figures; most line-24 'other (specify)' revenue has generic labels and cannot be classified operating vs non-operating (5-6% of operating revenue, shown on the page); no Medicare margin yet.
Relevancehigh — benchmarks the KH sample vs the full universe; adds payer mix
Our serieshcris_op_margin_median

Subsectorspharma distribution pbm
TickersCVS WBA MCK COR CAH
Geographynational
CoveragePer-NDC average price retail pharmacies actually PAY to acquire a drug, from a monthly survey of ~2,000+ pharmacies. The highest-frequency free drug-price series that exists anywhere.
If it movedWhat pharmacies PAY. Accelerating generic acquisition deflation temporarily EXPANDS pharmacy margin because reimbursement lags on the way down - and squeezes it when acquisition costs inflate on shortages.
Statsrows: 968,002 in the 2026 dataset alone · units: usd_per_unit
GapsRETAIL pharmacy acquisition cost — specialty and limited-distribution products are thin or absent (measured 2026-08-17: IMBRUVICA returns 0 rows, as do the generic/biosimilar molecule names APIXABAN, SEMAGLUTIDE, USTEKINUMAB, EMPAGLIFLOZIN and ETANERCEPT, while SITAGLIPTIN — a small-molecule generic — returns 56). So it reads the small-molecule generic-entry story well and the biologic story badly. Acquisition cost, not the retail or net price, and Medicaid-survey-based rather than all-payer. Naming is two-sided: brands appear under the brand name, generics under the molecule, and neither list alone is complete.
Relevancehigh — `classification_for_rate_setting` (G/B) plus the paired generic price make the generic-entry mechanism behind the 2026 CPI collapse directly measurable, 8 months timelier than anything else in the pack
NotesScoped and PRICED 2026-08-17, deliberately not built. The v1 cut: ~50 curated molecules (the IRA-negotiated 10, the GLP-1s, the largest recent patent cliffs), one server-side `starts with` query each, emitting a weekly median NADAC per molecule plus a brand-vs-generic spread. Measured, not estimated: 15 molecules took 39.5s (2.64s each) -> ~2min for 50 per run; 3,165 rows for 15 -> ~10.5k rows per run; the per-year dataset already holds all 32 weekly snapshots of 2026, so unlike the CMS quarterly file there is NO accrete-or-lose deadline. Corrects an earlier note in this file that priced this as a 1M-row NDC-crosswalk problem: server-side filtering means the full 968k-row file is never touched. Real cost is ~2h of collector (the shape is identical to cms_drug_spending) plus ~1-2h of one-time curation to verify both the brand and generic spelling of each molecule returns rows — and that list needs a match-report guard like `negotiated_match_report`, because a spelling that drifts silently drops a molecule from the median.

Subsectorsphysician staffing hospitals facilities post acute
TickersAMN CCRN HCA THC UHS
Geographynational / state
CoverageOccupational Employment and Wage Statistics: employment counts and wage levels (mean, median, percentiles) by occupation and geography. RN is SOC 29-1141.
If it movedA structural LEVEL: what an RN costs in Texas versus California, which is the baseline for reading a staffing company's bill-rate mix or a hospital system's exposure by geography. It cannot tell you whether wages are accelerating -- the quarterly ECI and the monthly Atlanta Fed tracker are what do that.
GapsNOT A TIME SERIES. The API returned a single annual point per series (2025) with "No Data Available" for 2023 and 2024 in the same request, and BLS's own guidance is that OEWS estimates are not designed for year-over-year comparison because the methodology and reference period change between vintages.
Relevancemedium - a structural baseline, not a signal
Our seriesN o n e
NotesREJECTED AS A DASHBOARD SERIES, kept as a reference. Reachable and cheap, so the rejection is not about effort. Two reasons: (1) the project's own chart rule is "JP reads rates of change, not levels... a level chart is context, never the headline" (CLAUDE.md), and OEWS has no valid rate of change; (2) charting a not-comparable-across-years series with a YoY transform -- which is what every other series here carries -- would manufacture a trend BLS explicitly says is not there. That is the failure mode, not a missed opportunity. REVISIT if a state-level wage LEVEL is ever wanted for a specific question (an AMN/CCRN bill-rate model, or geographic exposure) -- then pull it on demand rather than putting it on the weekly dashboard.

Hospital and payer price-transparency machine-readable files ↗Rejectedfreeeffort: high
Publisherhospitals and payers (CMS-mandated) · Federal gov
Cadencemonthly · lag varies
Accessmanual_download · json
thousands of scattered files; payer Transparency-in-Coverage files run to multiple terabytes a month
Subsectorshospitals facilities managed care
TickersHCA THC UNH ELV
Geographyprovider / payer
CoverageActual negotiated commercial rates by payer and service - the thing the commercial-rate PPI only proxies.
If it movedIf it were tractable it would replace a proxy with the real number. It is not, at this scale - so the commercial-rate PPI stays the tracker and free published research (Health Affairs, the RAND hospital price studies) supplies the levels.
GapsAn industrial-scale engineering problem, not a collector. The usable aggregations (Turquoise Health, Serif Health) are PAID.
Relevancelow as a build - recorded so it is not chased again
NotesREJECTED on effort, not on value. Revisit only if a free aggregation appears, or if the new CMS schema enforced from April 2026 makes the files genuinely uniform. TRIGGER CHECKED 2026-08-27 -- STILL REJECTED, and now on a better ground than effort. (1) Free aggregation: NO. Serif Health, Payerset, Turquoise and PayerPrice all gate bulk data behind paid tiers; PayerPrice's free items are lookups and an explorer, not a downloadable national aggregation. DoltHub hosts a transparency-in-coverage repo but not a maintained national hospital MRF corpus. (2) Uniform schema: NOT DEMONSTRATED. The spec did tighten -- CMS finalised new/removed MRF data elements and a strengthened attestation (45 CFR 180.50(a)(3)(iii)) in the CY2026 OPPS/ASC final rule, effective 2026-01-01 with enforcement from 2026-04-01. But a uniform SPEC is not uniform FILES, and no post-enforcement compliance measurement has been published. Careful with the number that circulates here: the widely-quoted "21.1% fully compliant" is PatientRights- Advocate NOVEMBER 2024 and says nothing about the 2026 schema. CMS is now auditing for accuracy, completeness and formatting rather than mere existence, which is itself evidence CMS does not yet treat the files as uniform. (3) NEW, and the reason to stop revisiting on the schema question: AHA's 2026-06-05 fact sheet notes the MRFs carry rates "without the algorithms and rules that health plans apply to those rates to generate the actual payment amount". So even a perfectly uniform file yields a negotiated rate, not a realised price. That is a STRUCTURAL limit, not an effort one, and it does not resolve with better schemas. AHA also notes the annual requirement churn itself impedes use -- and the CY2026 revision is the fourth, with CY2027 already in cycle. REVISIT CONDITION, REWRITTEN TO BE CHECKABLE (the old one was unfalsifiable prose and sat unwatched for four months after its own date passed): re-open ONLY on a named, dated event -- (a) a free bulk national MRF corpus with a maintained schema, or (b) a published post-2026-04 compliance study showing >80% conformance to the CMS template, or (c) CMS itself publishing a consolidated MRF dataset. Absent one of those, do not re-evaluate before 2027-04-01.
Inventoried2026-08-27
